Mazzoli tells hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini how punk helped shape her musical sensibility and why her long collaboration with librettist Royce Vavrek was essential to transforming Saunders's sprawling ghost story into an opera. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: How the Iran War Is Making Alaskans Both Richer and Poorer
general.summary: Oil prices have surged across the United States as a result of the ongoing war in Iran. This means higher costs for households in most states, but in Alaska, the state government is bringing in new revenue from its high oil production to offset those higher costs. Some of the revenue is then redistributed to Alaskans through the state’s unique sovereign wealth fund. general.title: Protein Craze Fuels an Investment Boom in Livestock Health
general.summary: Animal health companies are tapping into the protein craze, investing billions of dollars to build up businesses focused on making cattle, pigs and poultry healthier for human consumption.

general.title: ECB’s Lagarde Says Inflation Likely to Stay High in Near Future
general.summary: Inflation is likely to remain high in the near future, European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde told the Japanese newspaper Yomiuri Shimbun, adding that second-round effects so far are no worse than anticipated.

general.title: America's newest small business owners with no employees are off to a hot start in AI era
general.summary: New small business formation is rising for owners who can grow with AI serving in finance, marketing and design roles, eliminating the need for hiring.

general.title: AI Safety Advocates Make Gains After $110 Million Midterm Fight
general.summary: Candidates who favor stricter oversight of artificial intelligence racked up wins in key congressional races, aided by a pro-regulation political funding group backed in part by Anthropic PBC at a time when Americans are increasingly uneasy over the rapidly developing technology.

general.title: Young Travelers Are Warming Up to Cruises
general.summary: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg News travel journalist Brittany Chang explains why cruises are attracting more Gen Z and millennial travelers as higher airfare and hotel costs make all-inclusive vacations increasingly appealing. Chang tells hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that cruise lines are courting younger passengers with mega ships, entertainment, adult-only spaces and nostalgia, with some sailings costing as little as about $30 a day. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Economy and Democracy Drove the Blue Wave
general.summary: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Rutgers University's Ashley Koning says affordability, concerns about democracy and government corruption helped drive voters toward Democrats, with significant shifts among Latino, young and independent voters. Koning tells hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that Democrats now face pressure to deliver tangible results on affordability before the 2028 election cycle. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Berkshire Makes Record $9.6 Billion Buyback
general.summary: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Insurance Analyst Matthew Palazola breaks down Berkshire Hathaway's third-quarter results, including a record $9.6 billion in share buybacks and weaker insurance earnings. Palazola tells hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that CEO Greg Abel is putting Berkshire's massive cash reserves to work through buybacks, acquisitions and equity investments while maintaining the measured approach associated with Warren Buffett.

general.title: Top Turkish Regulators Taken Into Custody in Fund Probe
general.summary: Turkish authorities detained top officials from the country’s regulators on Saturday, local media reported, the latest executives to be caught up in a widening fund scandal.

general.title: Democrat shaping AI policy bought chip stocks despite backing congressional trading ban
general.summary: Rep. Josh Gottheimer disclosed new AI-linked stock purchases months after voting for a congressional trading ban, as Democrats prepare to regulate the industry.

general.title: US Jobs Surge Raises Odds of December Fed Hike
general.summary: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg Economics Chief US Economist Anna Wong says October's surprisingly strong jobs report showed hiring broadening into white collar, manufacturing and transportation jobs, strengthening the case for another Federal Reserve rate hike. Wong tells hosts Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo how the Bloomberg Price Project uses millions of alternative data points to provide an independent, more granular measure of US inflation. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Berkshire Hathaway Boosts Buybacks as Operating Income Slips
general.summary: Berkshire Hathaway Inc. spent about $9.6 billion to buy back its own shares in the third quarter, a sign the company’s executives viewed the stock as undervalued. But declining insurance underwriting weighed on its operating earnings in a mixed quarter for the company.

general.summary: Crypto’s extraordinary run of political good fortune in Washington has come to an abrupt halt. With Democrats set to control Congress following their midterm sweep, the industry faces the prospect of tougher rules and closer scrutiny of its ties to President Donald Trump.

general.summary: China’s economic planning agency flagged weak demand as a challenge for the country as policymakers study measures for next year, according to a statement Friday.

general.summary: SoftBank Group Corp. and ABB Ltd. are looking at carving out the Chinese part of a giant robotics deal as they explore ways to salvage a transaction blocked by Beijing, according to people familiar with the matter.

general.summary: Pablo Hernández de Cos, one of two candidates in the running to replace Christine Lagarde as president of the European Central Bank, signaled that monetary policy-makers should remain attentive to inflation risks emerging from high energy prices.

general.title: Trafigura Snaps Up Copper in Asia as China Faces Supply Crunch
general.summary: Trafigura Group has been buying large volumes of copper to boost sales into Asia as local supplies run low, adding to a scramble for metal that’s pushed regional premiums for spot cargoes to record highs.
